entry.title: Remove Shortcut Arrow Icons 2.0.0
entry.content:

entry.title: Automatic Folder Icons 1.0.0
entry.content:
Automatic Folder Icons

Put a folder.ico or favicon.ico file directly inside a folder, and Explorer shows it as the icon of that folder. Nothing else is needed: no desktop.ini, no registry changes, no folder attributes, and the mod never writes to your folders.

Before and after:

How it works

  • folder.ico takes priority. If it is missing or isn't a valid icon, favicon.ico is used, and then the original Windows icon.
  • favicon.ico can be turned off in the mod settings. This is useful if you have web projects, where many folders contain a favicon.ico.
  • Hidden icon files work too.
  • A folder that has an icon file shows the icon instead of a thumbnail preview.
  • Adding, replacing or removing the icon file is picked up within a couple of seconds while an Explorer window or the desktop is in use. If Windows keeps a cached icon, press F5 or reopen the parent folder.

Performance

  • Files, including ZIP and CAB archives, are skipped without touching the disk. Only folders are checked, with two small file lookups per folder.
  • Up to 256 recently shown folders are remembered and rechecked every two seconds, and only while Explorer is the active app and you are using the PC. Nothing is checked while you work in another app or are away, and the disk tree is never scanned.

Limitations

  • Only explorer.exe is affected. Other apps, including their open and save dialogs, show the original icons.
  • Only local fixed and removable drives are supported. Network paths, virtual folders, reparse points, cloud placeholders, paths longer than about 245 characters and icon files larger than 4 MiB are skipped.
  • After enabling or disabling the mod, some icons may stay cached until Explorer is restarted. The mod never restarts Explorer by itself.

entry.title: Simple Wallpaper Switcher 0.1.3
entry.content:
Simple Wallpaper Switcher

Screenshots

Solid Blurred
Acrylic Quick-menu

Your wallpaper collection, ready when you are.

Browse your wallpapers in a compact visual picker, choose a new look, and watch it transition onto your desktop.

Find your next wallpaper

See your collection as a grid of thumbnails. Browse folders with the breadcrumb menu, click a wallpaper to apply it, or use the keyboard to move through your collection.

Stay in the flow

Choose another wallpaper while a transition is running. The effect retargets to your latest choice, so you can keep browsing without waiting for each change to finish.

Make it yours

Choose from the shared Emberveil themes and set the picker background to Solid, Blur, or Acrylic. Pick a transition effect, or let Random choose one for you.

Wallpaper behavior

Applying a wallpaper updates the Windows desktop wallpaper setting. Windows keeps that image after the mod is disabled or removed, and applying an image replaces a Slideshow or Windows Spotlight background. The picker applies the image to the monitor under the pointer.

Get started

Set your wallpaper folder in the mod settings, then open the picker from its tray icon or keyboard shortcut.

The tray icon stays available while the mod is enabled. Disable the mod in Windhawk to stop the switcher.

Click a thumbnail to apply it. Use the arrow keys to move, Enter or Space to apply, and the mouse wheel to change pages. Click the magnifying glass in the breadcrumb, or start typing, to filter filenames in the current folder. Press Escape to clear the search.

Supported image formats: JPEG, PNG, BMP, and WebP.

entry.title: Cursor Scheme Extension 1.0.3
entry.content:
Cursor Scheme Extension

English · Русский

Cursor Scheme Extension replaces built-in application pointers with pointers from the selected Windows scheme. This includes middle-button autoscroll, the pointing hand, resizing, and text and table selection.

The mod uses the scheme already selected in Windows and picks up changes to it automatically. Transformed pointers are created and cached in memory.

Features

Cursor artwork: Windows and Office by Microsoft, W11 Concept by jepriCreations, Vision by IDarques.

Setting Controls
Hand Pointing hand over buttons, links, and other interactive elements
Resize Resizing panels, rows, columns, and objects
Move Dragging cells, ranges, and objects
Autoscroll activation The pointer after a wheel-click, before choosing a scroll direction
Autoscroll arrows All eight scrolling directions
Selection arrows Selecting rows, columns, or an entire table
Cell selection The cross over cells and when selecting ranges
Margin selection Selecting text from the left page margin
Vertical text input The horizontal mouse pointer in areas with vertical text

At the start of autoscroll, the pointer indicates vertical, horizontal, or both axes. Direction arrows use Alternate select (Up) from the Windows scheme, rotated to match the scrolling direction. Selection arrows use the same role. Transforms account for the pointer hotspot, and animated pointers retain their frame order and timing.

The interface is available in English, Russian, Spanish, German, Brazilian Portuguese, and Simplified Chinese.

Limitations

  • Replacement applies to recognized pointers displayed through Windows cursor APIs. The application controls whether autoscroll is available, its speed, and its direction.
  • Excel and Firefox draw their stationary autoscroll markers separately. These markers keep their original appearance.
  • Monochrome pointers that invert the background retain their original pixel rendering without smoothing.
  • Each mod load creates at most 128 replacement instances per process. Returning to a previously used scheme or smoothing setting reuses matching instances. When full, requests that need a new instance use the application's original pointer.
  • After disabling, the application restores its pointer at its next cursor update, usually the next mouse move. Replacement cursor handles remain allocated until the process exits so that pointers still used by Windows stay valid.

Platforms

Requires Windows 11. Runtime checks cover x86 and x64 processes on Windows 11 x64 with Windhawk 1.7.3. ARM64 has been compiled without a runtime check. Microsoft 365 and Qt WebEngine have not been verified.

Compatibility

Some of this mod's features may overlap with the following mods:

  • Chromium Cursor Remap — additional cursor replacement in Chromium and Electron.
  • Cursor Override — additional cursor replacement using .cur and .ani files.

Do not use multiple mods to replace the same cursors in the same application: the final cursor appearance may depend on the order in which replacements are applied.

Usage

Select a pointer scheme in Windows, then open the mod's Settings. Applications and processes selects the application families, and Pointer types selects the shapes to replace. Both must be enabled for a replacement to apply.

Family Coverage
Windows Native Windows pointers, standard controls, and Windows Forms
Office Desktop Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and classic Outlook
Chromium Chrome, Edge, Electron, and compatible embedded browsers
Gecko Firefox and compatible apps: cell selection, resizing, and vertical text
Qt Panel splitters in applications with a Qt interface

Under Application exclusions, below the family switches, add one executable name or full path per row. A name matches any installation of that executable; a full path matches one location.

Smoothing has separate switches for Autoscroll activation, Autoscroll arrows, and Selection arrows. Autoscroll smoothing covers all eight directions.

Links

  • Cursor Scheme Extension on GitHub
  • DSN Windhawk Mods

entry.title: Mac Island & Dock 3.3.0
entry.content:
New

  • Vice, a new theme in Colors (Look tab): a neon sunset over a dark night, like the city status bars made for desktops. Teal icons, pink highlights, Windows' Bahnschrift condensed font with the pill's texts in capitals, and a neon line along the island in every style. The power menu becomes a game's pause menu: Resume, the usual actions, and Wasted, which turns the screen gray before the PC shuts down (Esc cancels). ThemeId::Vice is added last, so the stored theme numbers keep their meaning; its colors blend in and out like the other themes (IslandTheme::vice, StepTheme). The font is UiFont's for the texts only while no font of your own is chosen, condensed through UiStretch, and FontsKey includes the theme so every text format is made again. The capitals use LCMapStringEx (the user's locale) for the same string that is measured and drawn. The neon line (DrawViceNeon) is drawn inside the island's shape: along its edge facing the screen's middle (round corners), and on a notch along the notch's whole outline away from the screen's edges (m_notchLine, the stroke's inner half kept by a layer masked with the notch's shape), with its two gradient brushes and the layer made once per render target and let go when the target changes. It draws only when the island draws anyway: no timer or frame of its own. Wasted is shown only with Shut down on and asks for confirmation like it; it is two windows of the island's thread (a gray LWA_ALPHA veil over the virtual screen that takes the keyboard and the mouse, and the word drawn while it moves, about 1.6 s), both destroyed before the same RunPowerAction(PowerAction::ShutDown, ...) the menu's Shut down uses. Esc, any key, a click or another window coming to the front stop it.
  • AI usage can also show other services' limits, read from a JSON file on this PC that another tool of yours keeps up to date, each with its name and icon on the pill and in the panel; "+ Add provider" in the panel adds more files (Apps and tools tab, off by default, #7307, made by Pedro). Code by Pedro (pedrospeckv), made on 3.2.0 and merged here. ReadCustomAiUsage reads one file on a local drive only (never a network path, up to 256 KB): one object, an array or {"providers": [...]}, up to kMaxCustomAi services with kMaxCustomWindows limits each, resets_at in seconds or milliseconds, an optional pill_name, updated_at and icon (a picture, .ico, .exe or an app's AppUserModelID, loaded with the existing local-drive check). It is read on the thread that already watches the Codex and Claude Code files (AiUsageThreadProc), a moment after the first change and not sooner than a few seconds after the last read, and the result is given to the main island (g_aiCustom). "+ Add provider" keeps more files in aiCustomList (AiCustomEntry: name, short name, file, icon); the panel's form switches animate like the Commands panel's. No network, login or token: the island only reads the file. The format is documented in the README's technical notes.

Fixes

  • Apps (launcher) opens its apps again when Windhawk doesn't run as administrator. Chrome, Brave, Office and other apps whose Start menu shortcut points into Program Files gave "The specified path does not exist" (#7521, #7360). The same goes for opening them from a notification, a command or Folders and places. The island runs in the 32-bit windhawk.exe, where %ProgramFiles% in a shortcut's path becomes "Program Files (x86)"; Explorer is 64-bit and reads it as Start does. OpensThroughExplorer (shell:AppsFolder and .lnk targets while IsWow64()) sends OpenApp, CommandOpenThreadProc, the notification's open fallback and OpenPath through ShellExecuteAsUser first, now passing the arguments and calling AllowSetForegroundWindow for Explorer's process, with the old way as the fallback. With Windhawk running as administrator, commands and Folders and places items that are a shortcut (.lnk) or a Start app now open through Explorer, unelevated, like the launcher already did; before, they inherited Windhawk's elevation.
  • Choosing a power mode in the control center no longer closes the island (#7539). PowerSetActiveOverlayScheme takes the GUID's address (const GUID*): passed by value, the 32-bit island pushed 16 bytes that the function, popping 4, left on the stack. Also reported in #7585.
  • Folders and places shows the own icons of shortcuts and programs, not the plain icon of their type (#7575). HasOwnFileIcon (.lnk, .exe, .url, .ico, .appref-ms) makes the shelf's and the folders' pictures ask for the icon (SIIGBF_ICONONLY) instead of a thumbnail, which these files don't have, with the thumbnails' option on or off.
  • On the minimized line, the timer's ring and its time stay together, with the clock after them (#7483). HiddenPillText puts the timer first, so its ring and its time stay together, and the clock goes after.
  • The timer filling the pill with color grows smoothly, also across the notches and on an upright Bar, and with the notches the minimized line shows the timer's real progress instead of filling too early. DrawFill has an asLine mode, so the minimized line shows the timer's real progress with the notches instead of a fill over the whole pill. TimerFillStep moves the fill by a quarter of a pixel of the bar's real length, not whole pixels, which made it creep (#7585).
  • Two separator lines no longer show side by side when the items between them have nothing to show, like what's playing with nothing playing (#7330). In Layout, a group that is on but has nothing laid out takes its line back (the slot is removed and the line's amount goes on to the next group that shows something), so two lines don't meet around nothing. Not done for the Bar's corners (linesSplit), where each line splits a side.
  • Faísca's games run at the screen's pace (up to 60 frames a second) and at the same speed whatever the frame rate, a Cloud jump that reaches a cloud lands on it, and her panel stays smooth while she sleeps (#7559). A panel's paced frames take kIdleFrameSeconds (a 30th minus 4 ms) and the window's kWindowFrameSeconds while a game plays: a frame exactly on a 60th was skipped when it came a hair early on a 60 Hz screen, so it ended near 30. The falling games (Fruit, Cloud jump) step in fixed kPetGameStep (1/240 s) pieces of real time (m_steppedAt, m_stepLeft, capped at 0.1 s a frame) so a late frame doesn't slow them. PetCloudLands lets a jump that tops out up to kPetCloudLedge short of the cloud land. The pet panel is paced while she sleeps too.
  • The Recycle Bin is watched and counted again a few times in the first minutes after the island starts or the PC wakes, and when a drive is plugged in, so it no longer keeps a wrong count after startup. kRecycleWarmupMs ({20, 60, 180} s after the island starts or the PC wakes, not the PC's uptime: Fast startup keeps it going) watches and counts again, and DBT_DEVICEARRIVAL does too (OnRecycleCounted).
  • Faísca's "Her size" goes up to 160%, for big screens at a small scale. kPetSizeMax goes from 130 to 160.
  • The visualizer's bars and the panels' animations keep their pace on a 60 Hz screen (they dropped to 30 or 20 frames a second). kVizFrameSeconds (0.0125 s) and kIdleFrameSeconds are a hair under a 60th and a 30th, so every frame of a 60 Hz screen, a little early, passes (exactly 1/60 kept every second frame, 30 a second; 1/30 gave 20).
  • With the pill upright (the Bar or the Island on a side), a count or a percentage beside an icon, like the Shelf's files, the battery, the volume, the Recycle Bin or AI usage, no longer draws a second clock over it (#7605). In Island::Render, the upright two-line clock branch ran for any slot with font 0; it now needs slot.item == IslandItem::Clock too. The same bug drew the second clock in #7577.
  • In What's playing's panel, the names of shuffle and repeat open above the button when the panel's bottom would cut them. MediaPanel::DrawButtonTip opens the tip above the button when the viewport's bottom would cut it.
  • The pill filling with color (a download, the battery charging or the timer) also fills a notch's curve down the screen's side. A notch at a screen's side (edgeLeft / edgeRight in NotchGeometry) curves down that side below its body; DrawFill's stretches stopped at the body's bottom, so that curve stayed empty. They now go down to the shape's bottom (GetBounds, already used for the shoulders at the ends), and the liquid front's wave spans that height. On a notch the fill's solid line (also the band sliding when how far isn't known, as with a copy or move) goes along the notch's outline (m_notchLine, the stroke's inner half kept by the fill's shape layer, clipped to the filled stretch) instead of a straight bar along the bottom.
  • In AI usage's panel, the day a limit starts over shows in the island's language, not in Windows'. AiResetTime named the weekday with LOCALE_NAME_USER_DEFAULT; it now uses DateLocale() like every other day or month name in the island (times keep the regional format, as before). It also showed for Claude Code and Codex.

entry.title: Taskbar Mini Folders 1.0.0
entry.content:
Taskbar Mini Folders

Adds mini folders to the Windows 11 taskbar, like the app folders on a phone. Each mini folder is a small tile that shows the first four icons inside it. Click the tile and a panel opens above the taskbar with everything in the folder. Click an icon to launch it.

Use it to group apps (Work, Games, Tools) and keep the taskbar short.

How it works

Every mini folder is a real folder on disk. By default it is %USERPROFILE%\TaskbarFolders\<folder name>. The mod creates the folder the first time you use + Add... or Open folder in it, not before. Whatever is in that folder shows up in the mini folder: shortcuts, programs, files and other folders. Hidden and system files are skipped. Items are sorted by name.

Using it

Action Result
Click a mini folder Opens its panel. Click it again, press Esc or click elsewhere to close the panel
Click an icon in the panel Opens the app, file or folder
Right-click an icon Open, Open file location, Remove from this folder (Delete for real files and folders)
+ Add... Pick apps or files. A shortcut to each one is created in the folder
Open folder Opens the folder in Explorer, so you can drag items in, rename or delete them

"Remove from this folder" sends a shortcut to the Recycle Bin without asking. For a real file or folder (not a shortcut) the menu item is called "Delete", because it removes the real item: it goes to the Recycle Bin, and Windows may ask you to confirm first. On a drive without a Recycle Bin (for example a network drive) the item is deleted permanently, and Windows asks first.

The file picker of + Add... starts in the Start menu programs folder, where most installed apps have a shortcut.

Settings

Setting Default What it does
Mini folders Apps, Work, Games The list of mini folders. Each has a name and an optional path
Folder path empty Leave empty to use %USERPROFILE%\TaskbarFolders\<name>. Any existing folder works, and environment variables are expanded
Position in the taskbar Next to the Start button Can also be after the last taskbar app, or at the far left edge of the taskbar
Mini folder button size 40 Size of the tile, from 28 to 56
Icons per row in the opened folder 4 Width of the panel, from 1 to 10 icons

Renaming a mini folder that uses the default path points it to a new, empty folder. The old folder and its contents stay on disk.

Files and folders the mod creates

  • The folder of a mini folder (by default inside %USERPROFILE%\TaskbarFolders), created when you first use + Add... or Open folder in it.
  • The shortcuts that + Add... puts into that folder.

These are your files. The mod never deletes them, so they stay on disk after the mod is disabled or removed. Delete the TaskbarFolders folder yourself if you no longer need it.

Performance

  • Folder contents and icons are read on a background thread, never on the taskbar thread, so a slow disk or a network folder can't freeze the taskbar.
  • Nothing runs in the background: no timers and no folder watching. The tile preview is refreshed when you open the mini folder or change it from the panel.
  • Opening the same mini folder again reuses the icons that are already loaded.

Limitations

  • Windows 11 with the new taskbar only. It doesn't work with the old taskbar restored by ExplorerPatcher or similar tools.
  • If you change a folder in Explorer, the tile preview updates the next time you open that mini folder.
  • Dragging items onto a mini folder is not supported. Use + Add... or Open folder.
  • The panel does not scroll. A folder with many items gets more icons per row so that the panel fits the screen. Items that still don't fit are not shown.

Tip: unpin the normal taskbar icons and keep everything in mini folders.

entry.title: Alt+Tab Flip 3D 1.8.0
entry.content:
• Renamed from "Alt+Tab Flip 3D (Vista Style)" to "Alt+Tab Flip 3D": the Vista stack is now one of many styles. The mod's id and settings stay the same.
  • New "Radial wheel" style: the windows' icons on the slices of a ring, around a disk with the app's name and the window title. Tab goes around it clockwise, moving the mouse points at a slice and selects it, like the weapon wheel of a game, and clicking a slice switches to it. The wheel fits any screen size and shape, grows with the number of windows, and the windows fly into their slices when it opens.
  • New Mica and Mica Alt backgrounds, made from the wallpaper like the material of Windows 11 apps, in the Windows light or dark mode (#7578).
  • New "Custom" frame rate limit, with a number of your own from 30 to 720 FPS (#6934).
  • The switcher moves to its monitor before drawing its first frame, so opening it on a faster monitor right after a slower one no longer runs at the slower monitor's frame rate (#6934).
  • The Icons and titles and Radial wheel styles show sharp app icons: the window's icon is read again from its app in a large size, instead of being enlarged from its small one.
  • The selection of the 2D styles stays visible with a black or very dark Windows accent color: a lighter shade of it is used.
  • Styles without thumbnails (Icons and titles, Vertical list, Classic, Radial wheel) stop updating the pictures of the windows once they're open, since they're hidden then, which saves GPU work.

entry.title: Spotlight Launcher 1.2.0
entry.content:
• Run the tools on your PATH. Type a program's exact name - git, python, cargo, code - and it appears below your apps, ready to run, with no Start menu shortcut to create. A partial name never lists them, so hundreds of tools stay out of the way. A tool installed later shows up after a reindex, and one whose executable carries no icon of its own uses the same generic application icon Windows draws for it.
  • Match app descriptions (Settings > Search, off by default). A search option that also matches the description Windows stores for a program, and shows it beside the app name, so a word that only appears there still finds the app. The text is the one its shortcut declares when it has one, and the program's own description otherwise. Off by default because a description is read from every program while indexing, which makes the first index slower.
  • Apps are ranked the way PowerToys Run ranks them. A match that covers a large part of the name, starting near its beginning, now ranks above one that merely contains the query. Frequency, pins and an app you pick after typing a few words still apply on top, so the list keeps learning from you.
  • Tools found on the PATH sit below the apps. A command never pushes the application you meant down the list.
  • Shortcuts that no longer lead anywhere are gone. A Start menu entry whose program was uninstalled, and a saved web link, no longer appear as a row with an empty icon. Game launchers such as steam:// are kept, and Microsoft Store apps are unaffected.
  • Microsoft Store apps always show their icon. The logo is now read from the installed package instead of asking the shell, so an app on another drive, an app that was never opened, or a cold icon cache no longer leaves a blank page. A small icon is no longer drawn tiny in the corner of the slot.
  • Classic apps show the icon their shortcut declares. Shortcuts that point at a console, an iconless launcher or a .cmd now use the artwork the shortcut names. A program with no icon of its own falls back to the generic application icon Windows uses, never to an empty slot.
  • Chromium web apps stay out of the way. An app installed from Chrome or Edge no longer appears while you search for the browser itself, but it is still listed when you type its name.

entry.title: Nimbus Menu 1.1.0
entry.content:
• New "Downloads" tab in Start: the newest files in the Downloads folder, plus files downloaded from the internet into any other folder (found with Everything).
  • Search box: select text with the mouse or Shift + arrows, and use Ctrl+A, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+X, Ctrl+V, Home, End and Delete.
  • Right-click on a file (search results and Downloads): open, open file location, copy path. "Open file location" for desktop apps in All apps too.
  • "End task" in the dock's app menu, following the Windows option (Settings > System > For developers), with a new setting to always or never show it.
  • Windows key: typing right after it now always goes to Nimbus' Start, also when the keyboard used to go back to the previous window. Pressing it again with Start open only closes it.
  • Apps whose window belongs to a helper process, like Steam, are now pinned with the right program and icon.
  • With Windows' transparency effects off, or battery saver on, the glass becomes a solid color instead of black.
  • Smoother rounded glass corners, and no more stutter when scrolling through all apps.
  • New homepage for help and suggestions: https://github.com/igoredm/nimbus-menu

entry.title: Desktop Weather 1.2
entry.content:
• The mod is now called Desktop Weather. It's the same mod, and your settings are kept.
  • New "What falls" setting: snow, rain, autumn leaves or cherry blossom petals. Rain splashes on top of the windows. Leaves and petals rest on top of the windows for a while and then fade away. They ride along when you move a window, and fly off when you yank or close it or sweep them with the cursor.
  • "Hide in fullscreen apps" now works on every monitor, not only the one with the focus: a fullscreen video on one monitor hides the snow there while you work on another one. It also recognizes more fullscreen players and games.
  • New "Also hide over maximized windows" setting (off by default), handy with an auto-hidden taskbar, where a maximized window fills the whole screen.
  • Choose the monitors: all, only the primary one, or a list of monitor numbers. Each monitor can have its own settings (what falls, how much, and where).
  • Choose the color of the snow and rain (presets or a custom color code), and the opacity of everything that falls.
  • New hotkey to turn it off and on, Win+Alt+S by default.
  • New "Hide for these apps" setting: hide it on a monitor while a window of one of the listed apps is open there.
  • It can come only for a season (for example from December to February) or only at certain hours. While it's off, it frees its video memory.
  • A new demo shows all four kinds of weather.
